original_record.question:
Each of the designs shown is initially divided into squares. For how many of the designs is the total area of the shaded region equal to three-fifths of the area of the whole design?
<image1>
original_record.solution: The fractions of the shapes which are shaded are $\frac{3}{8}, \frac{12}{20}, \frac{2}{3}, \frac{15}{25}$ and $\frac{4}{8}$ respectively. Of these, only $\frac{12}{20}$ and $\frac{15}{25}$ are equivalent to $\frac{3}{5}$. Therefore two designs ( $\mathrm{B}$ and $\left.\mathrm{D}\right)$ have threefifths of the shape shaded.
